title: Rear Quarter Panel Speaker — Convertible
introduction:
The speaker is the short part of this job; the rear seat and surrounding trim are its opening act. I work through those layers in order so each panel’s clips and locating tabs can be released deliberately.

This guide covers physical removal and installation, including seat access and the convertible flap checks needed during reassembly. It does not diagnose a sound complaint or prescribe electrical testing.

items.name: Vehicle configuration
items.detail: For convertible vehicles with SYNC and 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines. The loadspace-trim illustrations show LHD, with RHD similar, and the RH side, with the LH side similar.

items.name: Fastener tools
items.detail: Have tools that fit the speaker and rear-seat-backrest fasteners, plus torque equipment suitable for their specified installation torques.

items.name: Prevent remote starting
items.detail: Before service, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Prevent unauthorized starting
items.detail: After positioning the convertible top and front seats for access, switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle before dismantling. An engine accidentally started by another person during service can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to take these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Seat installation safety
items.detail: Follow every seat-removal and installation step and note carefully. Do not place objects between seat components and the vehicle body, or inside a joint within the seat structure. Incorrect installation can cause improper seat operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury.

items.name: Position the top and front seats
items.detail: Fully open the convertible top. Move both front seats fully forward to provide access to the rear seat.

items.name: Remove the rear seat cushion
items.detail: Use [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation). At the front of the cushion, press the locking tabs inward to release the cushion from the floor. The tabs must be pressed in before lifting; pulling without releasing them can damage them. Lift and release the cushion, then remove it.

items.name: Remove the convertible rear seat backrest
items.detail: Use [Rear Seat Backrest - Convertible](#/document/G1709034). With the cushion removed, locate the backrest-to-floor fasteners at the lower outer corners beside the side trim and remove them. Support the backrest while reaching the hooked locking clips behind it. Move each clip’s upper locking portion inward toward the upholstered side of the backrest to release it. Once the clips are released, lift the backrest upward to disengage it, then remove it. During installation, tighten the backrest-to-floor fasteners to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm).

items.name: Secure the parked car
items.detail: Park the car and apply the parking brake before positioning the top and seats or beginning the rear-seat and trim work. This cabin operation does not require lifting the vehicle.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The mounting-fastener tightening specification appears alongside removal, so it belongs in the reassembly plan from the outset.

edits.text: Remove the convertible loadspace trim panel using [Loadspace Trim Panel - Convertible](#/document/G1692610) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: With the rear seat backrest removed, position the seatbelt guide aside, release the clips and remove the upper loadspace trim panel. Next, release the middle panel’s clips, pull forward and outward to free its rear tab, position the front and rear safety belts aside, and remove the middle panel. Release the clips and remove the scuff plate trim panel, then release the clips and remove the lower loadspace trim panel. I use the linked illustrations to distinguish the clip locations from the rear locating tab: each needs its own release movement. The upper panel also has a specific installation sequence, described under installation.

edits.text: Remove the bolts securing the rear quarter panel speaker, disconnect its electrical connector as described below, and remove the speaker.
edits.why: In the speaker illustration, cyan identifies the speaker assembly, while magenta identifies the mounting bolts and electrical connector. The connector is the remaining electrical attachment after the bolts are removed.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector shown at the lower edge of the speaker. During installation, tighten the speaker mounting bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: The tightening specification applies to the speaker mounting bolts; the connector is disconnected and reconnected, not tightened.

edits.text: Install by reversing removal. Reconnect the electrical connector, position the rear quarter panel speaker and tighten its mounting bolts to the specification above. Refit the lower loadspace trim panel, scuff plate trim panel, middle loadspace trim panel and upper loadspace trim panel, re-engaging their attachments. Reinstall the rear seat backrest and then the cushion, reversing their removal steps and using the backrest-fastener torque specified in the preparation requirements.
edits.why: The upper panel needs more than a simple rewind: visually check the convertible flap and position it aside if required before installing the panel. Make sure the flap does not become trapped underneath it, then return the seatbelt guide to position. During trim, backrest and cushion installation, keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to occupants. I make that the final cabin check: a neatly fitted panel is only part of a finished job. When reinstalling the backrest, lower it into its mountings, reversing its upward removal, and pivot the hooked locking clips into engagement with their body catches. Confirm the clips are engaged and the backrest is seated before tightening the floor fasteners; keep belt webbing out of the joints.
